A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the existence of the Pd(IV)-Pd(II) catalytic cycle, but we cannot say that it is the only one.
the presence of two Pds in a Pd(IV)/Pd(II) catalytic system is not necessary for a catalytic cycle.
the Pd(IV)-Pd(II)-Pd(IV)-intermediate is the key intermediate of the catalytic reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a Pd(IV)/Pd(II) catalytic cycle is possible in the presence of a Pd-IV complex that is not very stable.
the use of a pincer ligand allows the generation of Pd(II)-Pd(IV)-Pd(II) catalytic cycles in Heck-type reactions.
the presence of Pd(II)- and Pd(IV)-species in the catalytic reaction can be detected by ESI-MS and that these species can coexist in the same solution.
